transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lila Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO, Celestia), Evan Brooks (Lead ML Eng), Jamal Ortiz (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand Celestia's ML infra, performance goals, security requirements, and what an experiment with Redwood PLG quickstart would look like. Customer interested in hosted API to start, potential Dedicated later for predictable throughput and data isolation; security and KMS/SSO questions noted.

Transcript:
00:00 Lila: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm lila from redwood - super quick intros?
00:05 Priya: yeah this is priya, i'm cto at celestia, we build inference-driven search for scientific docs. Evan and Jamal are here
00:10 Evan: hey all, lead ml eng
00:12 Jamal: jamal, sre - i'll be looking at network and infra stuff
00:15 Lila: awesome. Marcus is our systems se, he'll do the tech bits. Marcus you wanna do a 30-second?
00:20 Marcus: yeah, hi all. i'm marcus, focusing on latency profiles, batching, and dedicated deployments. today we'll cover quickstart experience, security, and typical ramp paths from hosted -> dedicated or private.
00:32 Lila: cool. high level, curious where you are in evals and what success looks like?
00:38 Priya: sure. we want to reduce query latency for our production search use case, current p95 is around 450ms on our in-house transformer; cost is getting high. we like the idea of a PLG first self-serve api to iterate quickly. success is 90% of queries under 200ms at 5k qps in peak, or a predictable path to get there.
01:00 Evan: and time-to-first-token matters for our UX, we track TTFT end-to-end. also we do embeddings for semantic match, so embedding throughput/cost is important.
01:10 Marcus: got it. quick question on current infra? are you using cloud GPUs or running on vms?
01:14 Priya: mixed - some model training on gcp, prod inference currently on k8s with a couple of nvidia a100s managed in-house. but scaling is painful.
01:22 Lila: thanks. ok let's walk through the quickstart with hosted api - it's the fastest path: signup, redeem free credits, call the rest or sdk, time-to-first-token normally under a few minutes for a basic sample.
01:32 Evan: how does the free credits work? is it per account or per org? and does it require any billing info?
01:38 Lila: good q — we provide a trial credit tied to the account; no billing required to start. credits can be used against text gen and embeddings. if you need org-level management we can link across teammates.
01:47 Jamal: on networking - we definitely have constraints: egress rules and want data to stay in our region. if we start hosted, will data transit out of region?
01:55 Marcus: hosted endpoints are region-aware; we can route to nearest region. for regulated workloads we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private with VPC peering.
02:03 Priya: for enterprise, our security team will ask about SOC 2, audit logs, key management - do you provide KMS/HSM integrations?
02:12 Lila: yes, we have KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. we also provide audit logs and RBAC in the console. i'll share the SOC2/ISO docs after the call.
02:22 Evan: perfect. one technical: how do you handle kv cache and prefix caching? we see a lot of repeated prefixes in search rerank work.
02:29 Marcus: we have automatic prefix/KV caching; it reduces per-token compute for repeated context. also continuous batching helps during bursts. quantization-friendly paths and kernel selection help on GPUs too.
02:40 Priya: nice. about model variants, can we pin to a version? we need deterministic outputs for a pilot.
02:45 Marcus: yes, you can pin model versions and rollout policies; we support canary and A/B rollouts. for determinism we can lock model+tokenizer versions. there is small transcription note: sometimes model names in docs get mis-typed - we'll make sure the exact artifact is in the PRD.
02:57 Lila: from a PLG perspective you can get started with our hosted api in minutes. typically teams redeem credits, run evals with sample prompts, and then we help size Dedicated if needed. common ramp pattern: hosted -> dedicated reserved capacity for steady traffic -> private only for compliance-sensitive customers.
03:12 Priya: what's the expected p95 latency on hosted for a 4k llm?
03:16 Marcus: rough range - for smaller models p95 can be under 100ms; for larger models 200-400ms depending on seq length and model family. batching/config matters a lot. we can run a baseline with your 1k sample queries to get a realistic profile.
03:28 Evan: ok that's helpful. cost question — how do you show unit economics? can we see token-level breakdowns?
03:33 Lila: yes console shows token-level cost and latency; we also give per-route dashboards and trace hooks. plus Optimize gives quantization and batching recommendations to reduce unit cost.
03:43 Jamal: about private deployments - does your on-prem package support air-gapped clusters? any special install?
03:48 Marcus: yes, we have an on-prem bundle for air-gapped installs and a private control plane option for VPC deployments. install involves our operator and some inventory, we provide the deployment playbook.
03:57 Priya: ok good. security review will want network diagrams and SAML/SSO details. do you support SSO?
04:03 Lila: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. we'll include those docs.
04:08 Evan: another technical concern: for high throughput embedding generation, how do you handle batching vs latency? we can't trade latency too much for throughput.
04:16 Marcus: we offer dynamic batching policies that are workload-aware; you can configure latency SLOs and the runtime will balance batching to meet them. also intelligent routing can route to cheaper model variants when latency budget allows.
04:27 Priya: are there any known gotchas when moving from hosted to dedicated — like breaking changes or a long migration?
04:33 Marcus: migrations are generally smooth; same API surface, same SDKs. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; we help with model compilation/quantization recommendations. we run a migration checklist to validate tokenization, kv cache behavior, and perf tests.
04:47 Lila: user story - we often send a quickstart repo with sample calls and a small benchmark harness. you'll get a script to measure p50/p95 and cost per 1k queries.
04:56 Evan: excellent. timeline: we want to run a quick experiment in the next 7-10 days. what's realistic?
05:02 Lila: redeem credits and run the quickstart today, Marcus can run a baseline with your sample dataset within a week.
05:08 Priya: ok. on procurement - if we like results we'll look at a 6-12 month reserved commit for Dedicated. need pricing for that too.
05:16 Lila: we'll share a pricing estimate; costs vary by reserved v on-demand and GPU type, and quantization can reduce footprint. we'll include example numbers.
05:24 Jamal: small nit - how are logs retained? retention policy?
05:28 Lila: default retention is 90 days for hosted but we have enterprise retention add-ons and you can export logs to your SIEM.
05:34 Evan: any issues we should expect with tokenization differences when switching open models? we've had mismatches before between tokenizer versions.
05:40 Marcus: good point — we version tokenizer artifacts and recommend pinning tokenizer and model together; we can provide conversion notes if you change families.
05:47 Priya: ok sounds like a plan. next steps recap?
05:50 Lila: sure - i'll send quickstart guide + free credits link, SOC2/ISO docs, SSO and network requirements. Marcus will run a baseline with your 1k queries once you share them; we'll aim for next week.
06:02 Evan: i'll drop a sanitized sample dataset and the eval prompts to the share link.
06:06 Jamal: i'll coordinate with our security team for the review slot.
06:10 Priya: one final — can we get a short note on the dedicated sizing assumptions? like gpu types and qps per gpu?
06:16 Marcus: yes i'll include a sizing spreadsheet showing qps per GPU family, expected latency ranges and recommended quantization.
06:22 Lila: perfect. thanks everyone.
06:24 Priya: thanks everyone, bye.

Notes (auto):

- Key risks: security/compliance sign-off, network/VPC constraints, desire for deterministic outputs.
- Follow-ups: share quickstart + credits, SOC2 docs, run baseline, provide pricing and sizing.

References shared during call:
